newsitem.title: USA: Mariners advance $5 million toward Seattle stadium.
newsitem.headline: Mariners advance $5 million toward Seattle stadium.

text.p: The Seattle Mariners will advance $5.0 million toward construction of a new baseball stadium to ensure the project remains on schedule despite litigation, officials said on Thursday.

The $5.0 million advance against a team commitment of $45 million will allow work to continue through mid-April, when the state Supreme Court is scheduled to get briefings in a lawsuit aimed at halting construction of the $414 million retractable-roof stadium.

Without the capital infusion the project likely would have been forced to shut down, making it nearly impossible to complete the project in time for the team's goal of opening the stadium in the 1999 season, said Paul Isaki, Mariners vice president of business development.

As it is, the stadium and its roof will not be completed by the original target date of April 1999. Officials are considering several options, including opening the stadium without its roof or a midseason move from the team's current home in the Kingdome.
So far work on the downtown Seattle stadium, including architectural drawings and demolition, has been funded by a loan from King County against revenues from an anticipated $336 million bond sale.

The county council is considering the possibility of issuing the bonds and putting the funds in escrow pending the outcome of the Supreme Court case. A vote could come early next month, said county council member Greg Nickels.
King County Executive Ron Sims said he was "very optimistic" the state would prevail over stadium opponents in the Supreme Court, as it has in lower court rulings.
Officials at a news conference did not say how they would keep work going after the current $5 million infusion ran out.
"This project will go forward," said county council member Jane Hague. "We will find the resources and the political will."
